slides.title: You read the same email **three times** and still don't know what to do first.
paras: The fix isn't a new app. It's letting AI do the sorting, so you only do the answering.

cards.title: Inbox triage
cards.text: You're my inbox assistant. Sort these emails into 4 groups: REPLY TODAY, HAND OFF (to: [WHO]), LATER (suggest a day), IGNORE. One line each: sender, what they want, deadline. Then draft a 2-line reply for every REPLY TODAY email. Emails: [PASTE SUBJECT + FIRST 2 LINES]

slides.note: Remove account numbers and private details before pasting.

messages.text:
1) Maria: can you send the quote for the kitchen job by Friday?
2) Supplier: invoice #2231 attached
3) Newsletter: 10 marketing trends
4) Tom (client): tap still leaking after the repair
5) Bank: your statement is ready

**REPLY TODAY**
• Tom: leak after repair. Unhappy client, fix first.
• Maria: quote for kitchen job. Due Friday.
**HAND OFF**
• Supplier invoice #2231 → bookkeeper.
**LATER**
• Bank statement → review Monday.
**IGNORE**
• Newsletter.

after.text: Hi Tom, I'm sorry the tap is still leaking. I can come back tomorrow between 9 and 11 at no extra cost. Does that work for you?

caption:
43 unread emails. One prompt. 5 minutes to know exactly what to answer first. 📥

Copy this:

"You're my inbox assistant. Sort these emails into 4 groups: REPLY TODAY, HAND OFF (to: [WHO]), LATER (suggest a day), IGNORE. One line each: sender, what they want, deadline. Then draft a 2-line reply for every REPLY TODAY email. Emails: [PASTE SUBJECT + FIRST 2 LINES]"

How to use it:
1) Paste only the subject and first 2 lines of each email.
2) Remove account numbers and private details.
3) Answer the REPLY TODAY group first, then move on.

I tried it on a sample inbox: the unhappy client went straight to the top, the invoice went to the bookkeeper, the newsletter went nowhere.
